commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for add and list
Remove task number tracking from Task.java
Change list to use the Task class
Handle cases for ToDos, Deadlines and Events
Update exception handling in main method
Fix more bugs in handleTask and handleMark
Apply Java coding standard to source and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Source and test files used inconsistent import ordering, line wrapping,
field modifiers, and test package declarations.

Standardize imports and line lengths, mark immutable fields final, use
idiomatic empty-string checks, add serialVersionUID, and align test
classes with their package paths.

These changes improve readability and keep source and tests consistent
with the SE-EDU Java conventions without changing behavior.

Define branch and commit-message rules based on the SE-EDU standard, and
require agents to read the skill before proposing or creating commits.

This makes future Git work consistent while preserving the repository's
authorization boundary for commits and pushes.

Allow users to search task descriptions without matching letter case while
preserving the original task order and display format.

Add JUnit coverage for matching tasks, no-match results, blank keywords,
and numbered search output.

Preserve master's JavaDoc and coding-standard changes while adding the
find command, case-insensitive description matching, and search tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure Checkstyle to detect coding style violations

commitResults.messageBody:
Task handling relies on some assumptions about non-null data. Violating
these assumptions can cause away from their source, making other
programming errors harder to diagnose.

Java assertions added to Task, TaskList, and Logic to document these
assumptions and detect violations when assertions are enabled.

Regular user input validation is still done with MiloException so
invalid commands are detected regardless of whether assertions are
enabled.

Parser.parseTask handles todo, deadline, and event commands together
with their validation and date parsing. The method is long and
deeply nested, making the command flow harder to read and
increasing the risk of changing unrelated parsing behavior.

Extract parsing of specific task types into dedicated private methods.
This improves readability and allows future changes to be made
independently without changing user-facing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract shared task-list formatting in Logic.java
commitResults.messageBody:
The list and find commands duplicate the logic for numbering tasks and
constructing their response messages.

Extract the shared formatting into one helper method that accepts the
response heading and task list. This keeps both commands consistent and
gives future changes a single formatting path to maintain.

Several command handlers overwrite their input parameters after
trimming them. Reusing parameters makes data flow less clear and
forces readers to track changing meanings for the same variable.

Keep the original input parameters unchanged and use descriptive
local variables for trimmed input values. This clarifies each
method's data flow without changing command behavior.

Storage closes its scanner and writer only after successful
operations. An exception during file processing can therefore leave
resources open and affect later storage operations.

Use try-with-resources for both file-handling objects so cleanup is
guaranteed on normal completion and failure. Preserve the existing
file format and error messages.

Storage restoration uses numeric indexes and string literals whose
meaning depends on the task file format. These values make the parser
harder to understand and risk incorrect edits when the format changes.

Define names for each record field position, minimum field count, task
type, and completion marker. Use those names during restoration to
make the storage format explicit without changing behavior.

Task handling contains important assumptions about non-null values,
valid task collections, successful parsing, and valid task indexes.

Merge the Java assertion changes from branch-A-Assertions, including
justifications for each assertion. Keep normal input validation in
place so user errors remain handled when assertions are disabled.

The code contains duplicated logic, overly long parsing code,
reused parameters, unsafe resource handling, and magic literals.

Merge the refactorings from branch-A-CodeQuality to improve
readability, maintainability, and resource safety while preserving
existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add rescheduling for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Changing a task's dates currently requires deleting and recreating it.
Add a reschedule command so users can update dates while retaining the
task's description and position in the list.

Support /by for deadlines and /from and /to for events. Allow either
event endpoint to change independently, preserving the omitted endpoint.

Reject completed tasks, todos, invalid task numbers, and invalid or
duplicate flags. Reuse existing date parsing and date-error messages.

Save changes immediately using the existing storage format and restore
the original task in memory if saving fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for rescheduling tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Verify deadline updates and partial event changes while preserving
descriptions and omitted event dates.

Cover invalid task numbers, missing or incorrect flags, duplicate
flags, invalid dates, and rejection of todos and completed tasks.
Check that rejected commands leave the original task unchanged.

Verify that updated tasks remain compatible with the storage format.

Allow users to reschedule deadlines and events without deleting and
recreating tasks. Support partial event updates, validate command
arguments, and restore the original task in memory if saving fails.

Include JUnit coverage for rescheduling behavior and error handling.
